name: Gemini Decision 1
note: Google's Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1, launched 11 Nov 2026) through OpenRouter's System One route (/api/v1/systemone, model google/gemini-decision-1; replies name google/gemini-decision-1-20261111), pinned to its one provider, Google AI Studio, with fallbacks off (provider.only [google-ai-studio], allow_fallbacks false). List price $0.10 per million input tokens, no output tokens (openrouter.ai/google/gemini-decision-1 and aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing, 11 Nov 2026); latency includes OpenRouter's own time. One choice question per request with up to 255 options (the API's limit; longer lists split by the league's rule); context 262,144 tokens, refused with 400 above it, never cut: League 1's largest stored request (229 options, 57,539 bytes) was 26,133 input tokens at the smoke test. Option ids are our move notations (unchanged), submitted in our seeded order; the model's effective order is Google's UTF-8 byte-sorted keys, as Google's docs state (aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api#choice; not verified by us), and an exact tie goes to the alphabetically first key (same docs); the runner plays the returned choice. OpenRouter answers some 429s (Google's per-tier token limit): retried as on every route. Probability maps: matches up to the switch (from #993, runner dab6da5) were played with no map check; from the switch on, runner map-check v2 (Zeki #4985): a map is usable only with exactly one entry per shown id, every value finite in [0, 1], summing to 1 within 1e-6 (no frozen sum tolerance existed; 1e-6 chosen 11 Nov for Gemini Decision 1 only); a failed map keeps the raw response and the returned choice is played, the exchange error names the cause ('map-check v2') and the decision stores no probabilities (probability_source NULL).
